walkthroughs.body_html:
K Na Ca Mg Al C Zn Fe H Cu Ag Au — most reactive to least.

Mnemonic: People Should Know Awesome Athletes Can Zoom Into Heavy Combat — Always Awesome.

The further left, the more reactive. Carbon and hydrogen are useful reference points — metals above carbon can't be extracted by reduction with carbon.

A more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from its compound.

Example: Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu. Zinc is more reactive than copper, so it kicks copper out of solution. The blue colour fades and brown copper appears.

It works for halogens too: Cl₂ + 2NaBr → 2NaCl + Br₂.

Electrolysis uses electricity to split ionic compounds.

Cathode (negative) attracts positive ions — metals or hydrogen form here.

Anode (positive) attracts negative ions — non-metals form here.

This is how reactive metals like aluminium are extracted from molten ores.

options: Silver
Gold
Iron
Platinum

mcqs.q: At which electrode do positive metal ions gain electrons?
options: Cathode (negative)
Anode (positive)
Neither
Both equally

mcqs.q: At which electrode are positive ions reduced during electrolysis?
options: At the cathode (the negative electrode) — positive ions gain electrons there.
Protons move from chlorine to sodium to balance the charges.
Positive ions are oxidised at the cathode by losing protons.
Positive ions are reduced at the anode because that's where positive things go.

mcqs.q: What is reduction in terms of electrons?
options: Gain of electrons (the oxidation number is reduced).
Reduction means a substance becomes physically smaller in size.
Protons move from chlorine to sodium to balance the charges.
Reduction means losing oxygen and oxidation means gaining oxygen — full stop.

mcqs.q: What happens to electrons when sodium reacts with chlorine?
options: Positive ions are oxidised at the cathode by losing protons.
Sodium and chlorine share an electron between them.
Protons move from chlorine to sodium to balance the charges.
Sodium loses one electron to chlorine; the resulting Na+ and Cl- ions attract electrostatically.
